newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates firm ahead of U.S. FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates firm ahead of U.S. FOMC meeting.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were steady to firmer on Monday on specualtion that the United States will raise interest rates at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.

"The overnights are unwilling to fall (too much) while there is some borrowing interest seen at the longer end," a local bank dealer said. Overnight money rates tend to ease on Mondays after rising ahead of weekends.
The overnight cash rate was little changed at 5-1/4 1/8 percent against 5-5/16 1/4 at midday on Friday while three month money jumped to 5-11/16 9/16 percent from 5-3/16 1/4 percent.
Although the market had discounted a 1/4 percentage point rise by U.S. rates, dealers still expected local money rates to move slightly higher if the rate hike materialises.
Trading in government paper was thin as bond dealers' view on the U.S. rate trend was relatively mixed.
"Half of the people still do not believe the U.S. will raise interest rate this week," a U.S. bank dealer said.
The one-week bill yielded 5.06 percent against 5.04 percent.
The longer-dated notes were generally unchanged with yields staying at their Friday levels. The seven-year note yielded 7.68 percent, the five-year 7.36 percent and the three-year 6.72.
